reason: A keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy, but it reads as a shrunk copy. The wordmark now sits on the teal circle, the content crowds the upper two-thirds, and the tiny legal line floats over a dead band at the bottom. B overscales the product, which dominates the canvas. It jams the headline against the bottom-left edge and shrinks the CTA into a small pill in the bottom-right corner, where it is buried. The legal text is squeezed into an illegible four-line wrap under the CTA, so hierarchy and spacing are broken.

A breaks the hierarchy: the headline is blown up to a two-line block running into the pills, the CTA pill is oversized and dominates, the subhead is shrunk and pushed into the top-right corner, and the flavour pills come out tiny, in reverse order and crammed against the right edge. B keeps the original's clean left-to-right banner structure: headline, subhead and pills are aligned on the left with the CTA balanced on the right. Its only flaws are minor: the decorative circles are enlarged and now take up more of the canvas, and the pill text is small.

A breaks the hierarchy: the 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' attribution is set as a heavy side column next to the quote, nearly as big and competing with it. The quote is squeezed into a narrow 4-line column, the logo is blown up and jammed under the quote, and the centered circle with the can looks detached and gets clipped at the bottom. B keeps the original's structure and feel: the quote has wide lines, the attribution sits small beneath it, the logo is bottom-left and the can is on the circle at bottom-right. Its only small flaws are that the circle is a bit large and dominant and that there's a slightly empty band between the attribution and the logo.

A is just the original shrunk uniformly: the quote is small for a 300x250 ad, the 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' attribution and the logo strip are illegibly tiny, the can's label can't be read, and the can sits jammed against the bottom edge. B actually rearranges the layout, with the quote mark set beside a larger 3-line quote and a readable attribution, but the quote is crammed against the top edge with almost no margin, the logo row floats on its own in the left middle, and the can still crowds the bottom edge, which leaves the bottom-left area empty.

A keeps the original layout intact: logo, SAVE badge, headline, body and CTA in a clean left column, with the product bag big and dominant. Its one flaw is the photo panel, which is now inset with thin margins on the top, right and bottom but sits flush against the left column, so it looks like a slightly awkward floating frame. B breaks the design. The product bag shrinks to a tiny thumbnail jammed next to a relocated logo, the photo background becomes an empty, meaningless blurry square in the middle, and the SAVE badge is shrunk and stranded on the left. Body copy, the empty square and the CTA are scattered across the bottom row, so the hero product is lost and the hierarchy is wrong.

A keeps the original's structure and hierarchy: the quote mark, the quote, the small gold attribution and the logo at bottom-left. Its flaws are that it reads as a shrunk copy, the backing circle is enlarged so the can sits off-centre near its right edge, and there is dead space in the middle-left. B breaks the hierarchy. It moves the attribution to a cramped column beside the quote and sets it bold and oversized so it competes with the quote. It pushes the logo up to sit right under the quote, wraps the quote into a narrow 4-line column with a large unexplained left indent, and leaves the composition lopsided with the circle cropped at the bottom.

A is broken. '20% off' wraps onto two lines and '20%' runs into the body copy. The body copy is a narrow, ragged column of one or two words per line, placed above and beside the headline, so the reading order is jumbled. 'WEEKEND ONLY' wraps, the bottle is jammed against the top edge, and the peach circle is cut down to a stub. B keeps the original's left text column (eyebrow, headline, body, CTA) and the bottle on the circle, all clearly structured. Its only flaws are minor: the bottle sits slightly low and off-centre on the circle, and the space below the CTA is a little uneven.

A breaks the layout: the oversized two-line headline crowds the left half, and the subhead is cut off from it and pushed to the top-right above the CTA. The bloated CTA competes with the headline, the flavour pills are reordered (honey/cucumber/blood orange) and jammed under the CTA against the headline's 'here', and the legal text sits on the peach circle. B mostly shrinks the original: it keeps the hierarchy, reading order, pill order and brand intact. But its pill labels and legal line are tiny to the point of being illegible, the content is inset with wide dead margins, the CTA is small, and the yellow circle now sits behind the headline block instead of the corner.

A is basically the original shrunk to fit: hierarchy and reading order are intact, but the pills and their labels are now tiny, there is a large dead band below the 'Reserve a spot' line, and the content block is pushed up under the oversized circle rather than reflowed for the taller canvas. B scatters the design: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits at bottom-left below the logo while the headline is top-right, the italic tagline is jammed into a narrow column beside the date, and the RSVP button comes before the vertically stacked pills, which are spaced unevenly. The 'Reserve a spot' line is cut off from its button, the can floats alone at bottom-left, and the missing-asset placeholder is enlarged, so the reading order is broken and there's no clear grid.

A keeps the original's structure intact: the quote and its attribution are grouped, the logo is bottom-left and the bottle bottom-right. Its flaws are a large empty band above the quote mark and an oversized, mostly empty maroon circle in the lower half. B breaks proximity by pulling 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' away from the quote into a cramped four-line stack inside the right circle. It also drops the logo awkwardly in the middle under the quote, which clutters the reading order, and leaves the bottle and circle crowded at the bottom-left beside dead space on the right.

A is just the square shrunk into the banner: the attribution and the SOLSTICE logo wordmark are too small to read, the jar is tiny, and there is a lot of dead space, so it fails both readability and fit to format. B actually rearranges the layout: the quote is larger with the quote mark beside it, the attribution and logo can be read, and the jar sits in its circle. But the quote is jammed against the top edge, the attribution runs onto the edge of the maroon circle, and the logo floats loosely mid-left instead of sitting on a clear grid.

A actually rearranges the layout for 300x250. The quote mark now sits beside the quote, the headline is set large and readable, and the attribution stays legible. Its flaws: the SOLSTICE logo floats on its own in the left middle with no alignment to the text column, the product glass is pushed low against the bottom edge, and the circles look cramped. B is the original shrunk down. The attribution and the SOLSTICE logo are tiny and unreadable, the quote is small, the large circle runs under the text, and the left and bottom areas are left empty.

A drops the SOLSTICE wordmark to y≈128, inside the green circle, and packs the can, headline, subtitle and CTA into the upper-middle. That leaves a dead band at the bottom and a tight headline-to-subtitle-to-CTA gap. B keeps the wordmark at the top like the original and spaces the can, headline, subtitle and CTA evenly down the taller canvas. Its only flaw is that the left end of the subtitle sits over the edge of the pale yellow circle, which is minor because that circle is a flat shape, not a busy image.

A keeps the original structure almost exactly for a nearly identical aspect ratio, which is correct here. Brand, headline, subcopy, pills and CTA are well spaced and aligned on the left axis. Its flaws are minor: the yellow circle now grows behind the headline and subcopy, and the pill labels and legal line stay tiny. B rebuilds the layout and breaks it. The headline is blown up into a three-line block jammed against the left and top edges. The CTA is oversized and competes with the headline. The subcopy sits above the CTA, so the reading order goes wrong. The pills are reshuffled, leaving BLOOD ORANGE alone on its own row, and the right column is cramped onto the pink circle with almost no margin.

A breaks the reading order: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits at the bottom under the headline. Its RSVP button has shrunk into a pill crowded in among the badges at the top left. The date, subtitle, URL and venue are stacked tightly with ragged left/centre alignments, and the logo is pushed off to the right with no anchor. B keeps the original hierarchy and order, but it is the 4:5 layout dropped centred into a square, not rearranged for the new shape. The badge pill text is still tiny, the lower third is mostly empty, and the placeholder box and legal text line up on no clear grid.

A rearranges the design properly: the quote mark sits beside a large, readable quote. Its flaws are that the attribution is almost as loud as the quote, the quote block is jammed against the top edge, the circle and can are cramped in the bottom-left, and the logo floats mid-right with nothing to line up against. B is just the square original shrunk to fit: the 'Ultra Tasting Team' attribution and the logo become illegibly tiny, the quote text is small, the top-left is dead space, and the can is crowded into the bottom-right corner.

A keeps the original's hierarchy, reading order, logo and steps intact, but it is basically the portrait layout padded into a square: a wide left margin, steps and CTA left small, dead space at the bottom, and the beige circle crowding the bag without bleeding off the edge as it did in the original. B is broken: the eyebrow 'POUR-OVER, PROPERLY' has moved down below step 02, step 03 has shrunk to tiny type and become separated from 01–02, the logo has shrunk to an unreadable dot next to the legal text, and the CTA now sits beside step 03 and competes with it, which scrambles the sequence and the brand.

A breaks the hierarchy. The 3-line headline and the oversized Shop Flavours pill both fight to be the focal point, the subcopy floats above the CTA away from the headline, and the flavour chips are out of their original order with Blood Orange left alone on a ragged second row. The chips and legal text also sit cramped against the peach circle, so it reads as a different design. B keeps the original layout, which suits a canvas only a little taller, with clear hierarchy, aligned chips and the brand intact. Its flaws are minor: the yellow circle has grown oversized behind the logo and headline, there is extra empty space at top and bottom, and the legal line is still unreadably tiny.
